newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds mostly lower in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds mostly lower in sleepy trade.

text.p: Mortgaged-backed securities (MBS) prices were mostly lower at midday Friday in somnolent dealings.
Discount mortgage coupons were 2/32 to 7/32 lower, while premium mortgage coupons were 5/32 lower to 3/32 firmer.
A New York MBS trader said that the market would probably remain quiet throughout the session. "We are in the middle of summer doldrums," he said.
While the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) was slated to meet next Tuesday, participants said Friday they did not expect the U.S. central bankers to raise official interest rates.
"People are ruling out any imminent Fed tightening, but a surprise (move) could hurt the market a little," the New York trader said.

One buysider, who agreed that activity in MBS had quieted this session, said mortgage-backed securities may be expensive because volatilities rose to a level where yield spreads should be slightly wider.

"By buying par coupon mortgages you are effectively shorting a call option, and with the higher volatilities this call option is not appreciating in value as much as it should have, " said See Yeng Quek, vice president of investments at Conseco Capital Management in Carmel, Indiana.
"Cusp coupons -- that is, 8.0 percents and up -- are very, very rich. Basically, spreads are tight relative to the risk being taken by investors," he said.

Among 30-year 7 1/2-percent MBS, Government National Mortgage Association bonds fell 4/32 to 101-6/32 to yield 7.34 percent, Freddie Macs lost 4/32 to 101-13/32 for a yield of 7.28 percent and Fannie Maes declined 3/32 to 101-12/32 to yield 7.24 percent.
In the meantime, the 10-year Treasury note fell 5/32 to 98-28/32 to yield 6.28 percent.
